claim: Anime sells size by putting a known object beside an unknown one, never by focal length. Reach for it the moment the frame has to feel vast or the subject has to feel small inside it.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: tiny distant figure, person in the distance for scale
parked car in frame, bus in the background
tall building alongside, skyscraper in background
distant horizon line, vast open expanse
colossal structure looming, giant object in background, towering scale

review.issue: human_figure ("tiny distant figure, person in the distance for scale") cannot do anything here: the subject sentence already contains "crowd", so distant human figures are in every single panel including the control. "for scale" is meta-instruction prose that renders nothing, and adding a person also contradicts "solo".
review.fix: Either mark human_figure unrenderable against a crowd subject, or replace it with a cue the subject does not already supply — e.g. "lone figure on empty pitch, vast empty space" — and cut "for scale" from the tag list. Same trim for the others: keep "parked car", "skyscraper in background", "distant horizon", "colossal structure" and drop the explanatory tail.

look_at: vehicle/building/giant_object anchor scale; the tower dwarfs the stadium as intended.
